activities.anchor: pointed at buttons, headlines and prices
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the casual shortcut's product
activities.name: abTheatrePredict

config.q: Done casually — tiny samples, forty metrics, stopping the moment p dips below 0.05 — an A/B test produces what?
choices: Confident nonsense, manufactured with impressive efficiency
config.why: Each casual shortcut quietly converts the error budget into noise — the machinery is only as honest as its pre-commitments.

activities.anchor: Flip a fair coin for every user
activities.caption: true or false — where the causal power lives
activities.name: abCoinJudge

statements.s: The randomisation IS the design — comparing post-hoc groups is observational, self-selected and confounded.
statements.why: The causal power lives in the randomisation, nowhere else.

statements.s: An A/B test is just 'compare the groups afterwards'; the design is decoration.
statements.why: Self-selected feature-finders versus everyone else is exactly the confounding the coin flips exist to remove.

statements.s: Randomisation balances the confounders you never thought to measure.
statements.why: Balance in expectation covers the unknown as reliably as the known.

statements.s: Weekly users buy more than casual ones, so the app causes purchasing.
statements.why: Or purchasers use the app more — the observational arrow points both ways.

activities.caption: score the lift — the arithmetic in order
activities.name: abScoreOrder

config.prompt: A runs 10.0%, B runs 11.0%, 10,000 users each — score the difference, in order:
items: Read the arms: 1,000 of 10,000 converted in A; 1,100 of 10,000 in B
The difference's SE: √(0.0031² + 0.0031²) ≈ 0.0044 — two wobbles combined in quadrature
One-sided p ≈ 0.012 — the mundane world struggles to account for it
config.why: At a 0.5-point lift instead: z ≈ 1.14 and p ≈ 0.13 — indistinguishable from noise at this n.

activities.caption: two ways to be wrong — file the damage
activities.name: abCostSort

config.prompt: Two ways a test can be wrong — file each consequence:

items.label: a change ships that does nothing — complexity added forever
the null was true but the test crossed the threshold by luck
the effect was real but the test missed it

config.why: The 0.05 threshold is a convention, not a law — match it to the decision's price and report the interval, not just a verdict.

activities.anchor: re-run or extend promising tests before scaling them
activities.caption: the headline vs the replication — drag the divider
activities.name: abWinnerCompare

config.prompt: Same test, second look — drag the divider:

after.label: the replication
after.text: landed lower — selection had picked a lucky draw; winners slide back toward the mean

config.why: Selection picks the lucky ones: expect the follow-up to land below the original estimate.

activities.anchor: more likely than not, the dashboard shows a victory that is pure noise
activities.caption: call the odds of a phantom winner
activities.name: abTwentyEst

config.prompt: Twenty genuinely null metrics tested at the 0.05 threshold — what is the chance that at least one 'wins'?
config.why: 1 − 0.95²⁰ ≈ 64% — one pre-registered comparison keeps the 5% promise; twenty opportunistic ones spend the whole budget.
config.context: Bonferroni divides the threshold; false-discovery-rate control limits the share of winners expected to be false — both spend power.

activities.anchor: from Kohavi's two decades of running experiments at Microsoft and Bing
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the launch postmortem
activities.name: abDesignSpot

config.prompt: One line of this postmortem is wrong — click it:
lines: A confounded assignment cannot be rescued by any test.
A broken funnel invalidates every downstream number.
A novelty spike, read as a trend, will evaporate at scale.
A metric chosen after seeing the data still counts — the statistics are the same.
The majority of surprising 'wins' evaporate under scrutiny of design, not of statistics.
config.correction: A metric chosen after seeing the data has already spent the error budget — no statistical machinery can give it back.
config.why: Design, not statistics, is where these contests are won or lost.

activities.anchor: it regresses out the part of the metric predictable from before the experiment started
activities.caption: call CUPED's discount
activities.name: abCupedEst

config.prompt: With CUPED at a pre/post correlation of 0.5, the required sample shrinks by what percentage?
config.why: Variance scales with (1 − ρ²): 0.5 cuts the needed n by a quarter; near 0.7 is routine for engagement metrics.
config.context: One idea that let platforms run tests they previously could not afford.
